thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected for dedicated-eu3 pool — streaming stalls observed; SLO p99 breached for last 5m (alerting: latency_slo:dubious) :rotating_light:
Eric (oncall): seeing it too, p95 up ~2x and p99 is huge. queues_depth metric hitting 900/1000.
Jen (SRE): confirmed: dedicated-eu3 pool 3/4 hotshot nodes warmed, but warmup handshake lagging. Warmup failures = 18 in 5m.
Maria (prod): any customer-visible errors? We got a SEV ticket from customer: "chat responses stall then 504".
Eric (oncall): yes, a few 504s from streaming sessions. Most are elevated latency, some aborted streams.
Alex (runtime): initial look: autoscaler requested 5 slots 6m ago, only 2 allocated due to slow handshake with cold pools. Handshake latency is 30s+ for slot init.
Ira (PM): are we hitting any global capacity cap or cloud quota?
Jen (SRE): no global quota — it's purely pool-level saturation. The pool has lots of long-lived KV caches pinned by tail requests; eviction hasn't reclaimed prefix caches fast enough.
Ops Bot: metric snapshot attached: 
```
pool: dedicated-eu3
queued_requests: 1240
active_slots: 48/50
warmup_inflight: 9
handshake_failures: 18
p95_latency: 1.9s -> baseline 0.8s
p99_latency: 6.3s -> baseline 1.1s
streaming_stalls: 83 events / 10m
```
Eric (oncall): immediate mitigation ideas? Can we throttle low-priority tails or move non-critical customers to hosted fallback?
Alex (runtime): we have a per-customer routing policy ready. Can trigger emergency reroute to hosted model variants for non-enterprise tiers. That will free 20-30% capacity.
Jen (SRE): also can enable fast-evict for KV caches in that pool to free memory; risk: increased coldstarts but will reduce handshake failures.
Maria (prod): prioritize customer impact — which customers are on that pool? I have a list, small set of enterprise and many small ones. SEV ticket is enterprise. We should avoid moving enterprise traffic if possible.
Ira (PM): agreed, prefer moving non-enterprise first. Notify customers after mitigation.
Eric (oncall): executing: 1) trigger routing reroute for tier=standard -> hosted fallback (Alex), 2) enable fast-evict for dedicated-eu3 (Jen), 3) increase warmup concurrency to 6 (Alex).
Alex (runtime): starting reroute now — applying routing policy change. Will post when done.
Jen (SRE): enabling fast-evict now, eviction TTL set to 30s from 5m. Monitor for regressions.
Ops Bot: reroute change applied: 27% traffic moved to hosted fallback for standard tier.
Alex (runtime): warmup concurrency bump applied. Warmup inflight down from 9 -> 5 currently. Handshake latency improving to ~12s.
Eric (oncall): any immediate change in queued requests?
Ops Bot: queued_requests dropping: 1240 -> 720 over 3m after reroute. p99 latency trending down to 3.0s.
Maria (prod): good, but still above SLO. Keep monitoring and prepare for customer comms.
Ira (PM): can we also temporarily increase reserved capacity (burst) for the pool? What's the deployment lead time?
Alex (runtime): reserved burst can be requested, but spin-up takes ~4-6m for additional nodes; I can request now.
Jen (SRE): note: if we add nodes they'll require cold KV warming; with fast-evict we might benefit from fresh KV load but handshake will still be a slight ramp.
Eric (oncall): request burst now, Alex?
Alex (runtime): requested +6 nodes to dedicated-eu3. Provisioning started.
Ops Bot: provisioning events: node_create_1 started; node_create_6 started. Estimated ready ~5m.
Jen (SRE): monitoring streaming stalls for reduction. Also setting temporary throttles on tail-priority queues to prevent starve loops.
Maria (prod): updating SEV ticket: "We observed streaming stalls and elevated latency; engineering is mitigating via traffic reroute and capacity bump. Will follow up in 15m."
Ira (PM): good. Also flag for postmortem: why did handshake latency spike? Is KV eviction too conservative?
Eric (oncall): once nodes come up we should evaluate warmup success rate and handshake health.
Alex (runtime): new nodes reporting ready: nodes +6 live. Warmup handshake success rate moving from 60% -> 92% over the next 3m.
Ops Bot: queued_requests -> 110; p99_latency -> 1.2s, p95 -> 0.85s. streaming_stalls -> 4 events/10m. SLO near restored.
Jen (SRE): throttles and fast-evict rolling back? I'd prefer keep fast-evict until we verify sustained stability for 10m.
Eric (oncall): agree keep for now.
Maria (prod): customer SEV updated: they confirm improved response times. No longer seeing 504s.
Ira (PM): thanks. Assigning follow-ups: - Alex: run warmup handshake dry-run and harden handshake timeouts. - Jen: own postmortem on eviction policy and orchestration. - Eric: coordinate customer comms draft with Maria.
Eric (oncall): noted. I'll ping here when postmortem doc created.
Jen (SRE): quick root-cause hypothesis: burst of tail-heavy workloads + large pinned KV caches + autoscaler not reacting due to handshake backpressure -> delayed slot admission -> p99 spike. Need longer-term fixes: predictive pre-warm for expected burst patterns, reduce handshake blocking, better cache eviction heuristics.
Alex (runtime): also consider transient fallback to quantized model variants that use less memory as a stop-gap during burst events.
Ira (PM): adding to our backlog. We'll prioritize a runbook update so oncall can execute reroute + fast-evict faster next time.
Ops Bot: Incident resolved: SLOs restored to within thresholds at 1710568670. Follow-up tasks created in /incidents/1710567890.
Eric (oncall): thanks everyone. Closing live triage. Will schedule postmortem meeting. :thumbsup:
